summary: Obfuscated preinstall loader executes opaque payload on npm install
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node preinstall.cjs`, which runs automatically on `npm install`. preinstall.cjs is a single ~311 KB line consisting of a `Function(...)` constructor over a heavily obfuscated program: a seeded PRNG/XOR string decoder (`fJyK0L`) operating on a packed alphabet string (`jVDbNW`), a numeric opcode table (`wKc07cB`), and a control-flow-flattened dispatcher. All strings, destinations, filesystem paths, and command invocations are reconstructed only at execution time, so the actual behavior is not visible in source. The package's shipped `main` is an unrelated thin AI-client stub, making the preinstall loader the substantive payload of the package. The combination of a lifecycle-hook `Function()` loader over a 311 KB opaque, control-flow-flattened blob has no benign explanation — ordinary native-build and license-check tooling ships readable source — and gives whoever published the package arbitrary code execution on every installer's machine at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
